Test Data: No session or token | Target URLs: /invoices | /ap/invoices/queue | /reports/monthly/may-2026 | /invoices/501
Test Steps:
1. Open a fresh browser session with no active login
2. Navigate directly to /invoices
3. Navigate directly to /ap/invoices/queue
4. Navigate directly to /reports/monthly/may-2026
5. Navigate directly to /invoices/501
Expected Result: All protected pages redirect to the login page. No content from protected areas is rendered. API endpoints return 401 Unauthorized with no data payload.

Title: SQL injection attempt in login form is safely handled
Preconditions: Application login page is accessible
Test Data: SQL Injection Payload — Email field: ' OR 1=1 -- | Password field: anypassword123
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to the login page
2. Enter in the email field: ' OR 1=1 --
3. Enter password: anypassword123
4. Click Login
Expected Result: Login is rejected. System returns a standard error message: 'Invalid email or password.' No unintended data is returned. No server error or stack trace is exposed.

Title: Upload a file with malicious content disguised as PDF
Preconditions: Vendor VEND-001 is logged in; invoice form is open
Test Data: Vendor ID: VEND-001 | PO: PO-2026-045 | Invoice: INV-TC-SEC-004 | Amount: $2,500.00 | Malicious File: malicious_script.js renamed to invoice_doc.pdf
Test Steps:
1. Log in as vendor: vendorA@testcorp.com
2. Navigate to Invoice Submission and fill all required fields (PO: PO-2026-045, Amount: $2,500.00)
3. Upload the file: malicious_script.js renamed as invoice_doc.pdf
4. Click Submit
Expected Result: File is rejected. System validates file content not just extension. Error message: 'Invalid file type. Only valid PDF documents are accepted.' No file is stored on the server.

Title: Session token is invalidated on logout
Preconditions: Vendor VEND-001 is logged in
Test Data: Vendor: VEND-001 | Email: vendorA@testcorp.com | Session token captured from browser dev tools before logout | Target endpoint: GET /invoices/501
Test Steps:
1. Log in as vendor: vendorA@testcorp.com
2. Capture the active session token from browser dev tools (Network tab or Application > Cookies)
3. Log out of the portal
4. Using the captured token send a direct API request to GET /invoices/501
Expected Result: API returns 401 Unauthorized. Session token is invalidated server-side upon logout. The captured token cannot be reused to access any protected endpoint.

Title: AP approval page is inaccessible to vendor via direct URL
Preconditions: Vendor VEND-001 is logged in
Test Data: Vendor: VEND-001 | Email: vendorA@testcorp.com | Target URL: /ap/invoices/INV-TC-007/approve | Invoice INV-TC-007 current status: Approved
Test Steps:
1. Log in as vendor: vendorA@testcorp.com
2. Navigate directly to: /ap/invoices/INV-TC-007/approve via the browser URL bar
3. Attempt to trigger the approval action
Expected Result: Access is denied. Page returns 403 Forbidden or redirects vendor to their own dashboard. No approval action is performed. Invoice status remains unchanged.

Title: Monthly report generates within acceptable time under concurrent AP user load
Preconditions: QA environment has at least 500 invoice records for May 2026; performance test tool is available (e.g. JMeter or k6)
Test Data: Concurrent users: 50 AP users | Report period: May 2026 | Dataset size: 500 invoice records | Acceptable response time: report loads within 5 seconds under load | Test tool: JMeter or k6
Test Steps:
1. Configure a load test script simulating 50 concurrent AP users each requesting the May 2026 monthly report simultaneously
2. Execute the load test
3. Measure response time for each request
4. Monitor server CPU and memory during the test
5. Validate report data accuracy for a sample of 5 responses
Expected Result: All 50 concurrent report requests complete within 5 seconds. No request times out or returns an error. Report data is accurate and consistent across all responses. Server CPU remains below 80% throughout the test.

Title: Invoice submission remains stable under concurrent vendor load
Preconditions: QA environment is running; 20 vendor test accounts are available; 5 active POs exist
Test Data: Concurrent vendors: 20 (VEND-001 through VEND-020) | POs: PO-2026-045 to PO-2026-049 (4 vendors per PO) | Invoice amounts: $1,000 to $5,000 | Attachments: invoice_valid.pdf (2 MB each) | Acceptable response time: submission completes within 3 seconds | Test tool: JMeter or k6
Test Steps:
1. Configure a load test script simulating 20 concurrent vendor users each submitting a unique invoice simultaneously
2. Each vendor submits against their assigned PO with a unique invoice number (INV-PERF-001 through INV-PERF-020)
3. Execute the load test and measure submission response time per request
4. After the test verify all 20 invoice records exist in the database
Expected Result: All 20 concurrent invoice submissions succeed without errors. Each submission completes within 3 seconds. All 20 invoice records are created with correct vendor IDs, PO references, amounts, and status 'Submitted'. No data corruption or duplicate records occur.
